title: Property Tax Growth Allowance in Rural Home Loans Escrow Projections
content:
In a Rural Home Loans escrow projection, the property tax bill is projected with a growth allowance.

## Rule

The property tax bill is projected with a growth allowance: the earlier bill is the property tax paid between 12 and 24 months before today, and when the latest property tax bill is at least 5 percent above that earlier bill, the allowance is 6 percent; when it is above the earlier bill by less than 5 percent, the allowance is 2.5 percent; when it is not above the earlier bill, or no property tax was paid between 12 and 24 months before today, there is no allowance; the projected property tax is the latest bill increased by the allowance, rounded to the cent.

## Terms

- **Latest property tax bill:** the most recent property tax disbursement paid from escrow.
- **Earlier bill:** the property tax disbursements paid from escrow dated after the same calendar day 24 months before today and on or before the same calendar day 12 months before today, added together.
- **Increased by the allowance:** the latest bill plus the allowance percentage of it, rounded to the cent.

## Allowance table

| Latest bill compared with the earlier bill | Allowance |
|---|---|
| at least 5 percent above | 6 percent |
| above, by less than 5 percent | 2.5 percent |
| not above (equal or lower) | none |
| no earlier bill in the window | none |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical earlier bill of 2000.00)

| Latest bill | Rise | Allowance | Projected property tax |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2100.00 | exactly 5 percent | 6 percent | 2226.00 |
| 2099.99 | just under 5 percent | 2.5 percent | 2152.49 |
| 2000.00 | none | none | 2000.00 |
| 1950.00 | a fall | none | 1950.00 |
